title: Lesson 70 - It Seems More Complicated Than That

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The weekly overdue counts are ten, nine, eight, nine, seven, seven, six and six. The evidence seems to suggest improvement, but not a smooth decline.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Agreed. It’s possible that shorter check-ins helped the team focus, especially because the team lead noticed that effect.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: One likely explanation is the new owner list. Every action had one named person after week two, so unfinished work became easier to follow up.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Why call that `likely` rather than simply `possible`?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The notes connect two recovered items directly to owner clarification. That is still limited evidence, but it links a mechanism to specific cases.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: We can’t rule out the written agenda either. The team began circulating it before meetings in week three, and the count fell again afterward.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: That doesn’t necessarily mean the agenda caused the fall. Week four rose from eight to nine even though the agenda was already in use.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: True. The result may depend on how consistently the team used all three changes, not on whether a document technically existed.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: There is also a workload note: incoming requests were lower in weeks seven and eight.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Then lower workload is a plausible contributor to the final count of six. Do we know whether the size of the action items changed?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: No. The log counts items, not effort, urgency or project importance. Six large overdue items could represent more work than ten small ones.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: So the measurement choice matters. What can we still say with reasonable confidence?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Over eight weeks, the recorded count fell from ten to six while meeting length, agenda use, ownership and follow-up changed. That trend is directly documented.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: And what is more tentative?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The shorter format may have contributed, but the evidence cannot separate its effect from the other changes or lower late-period workload.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Could the first week have been unusually bad?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: We can’t rule that out because there is no earlier baseline. Comparing only week one and week eight may exaggerate a normal fluctuation.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That may be true. However, the middle weeks mostly move downward, so the pattern is not based on the endpoints alone.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: A more accurate conclusion is: this team’s bundled process change was followed by fewer recorded overdue items, and shorter meetings are one plausible contributor.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Good. We can revisit causal weight only if we obtain a longer baseline, stable workload measures or a comparison that changes one feature at a time.
